title: Ask the audience to finish it
statement: Some posts ask the audience to finish one part of the work (pick the music, name it, caption it) instead of announcing.
evidence: one creator's top post was a pick-the-music ask (13,173 views, 319 bookmarks) against a 517 median; a brand's name-someone prompts drew up to 905 comments.

title: Stake in the first 125 characters
statement: Line 1 of an Instagram caption carries the stake inside the first 125 characters (2,200 max), and each platform gets its own caption rather than one pasted everywhere.
evidence: Platform truncation spec (about 125 characters before 'more') applied as a pack copy rule.

sources.locator: Instagram, last 30 days; How to apply, last line

notes: X counts every link as 23 characters. | Merged: Line 1 of the caption names a concrete money, client or deadline stake that a viewer would forward to someone. [inferred; own channel: 5 interactions and zero shares on 2,288 Reels views in 30 days; the caption fix is untested.] | skills/social-video/SKILL.md asks for the stake in the first 125 characters (prose); lint_shotlist.send_line warns on a missing send line in the script, not the caption.

title: Covers: 4 words, readable at 120 px
statement: A cover or poster frame carries at most 4 words and one subject, reads at 120 px wide, uses real type (never image-model text), and keeps words and subject centred for the 3:4 profile-grid crop.
evidence: Pack cover rule; the 3:4 grid crop and the 1280x720 thumbnail are platform specs.
notes: Only the word count is checked; upload a custom thumbnail for every YouTube video (search, channel grid and suggested views depend on it). | Merged: A cover or thumbnail has one subject and at most 4 words that still read when the cover is scaled to 120 px wide; YouTube thumbnails are 1280x720 and vertical covers 1080x1920 with subject and words centred. [house; pack cover rule; the story linter enforces the 4-word poster limit.] | Profile grids crop vertical covers (to 3:4 on Instagram at the time of writing), so keep the subject central. The 120 px read test itself is manual.

title: CTA: one verb, one destination
statement: A CTA states one verb and one destination in the viewer's words, with urgency only if true and no 'free', '100%' or 'guaranteed' unless literally true and approved.
evidence: Pack wording rules; a CTA asking for two things is a listed ad failure.
notes: Set today by: patterns/ctas.json wording.rules (a pack default outside mp plan). | On a launch platform that bans vote requests, ask the viewer to try it, never to vote (ctas.json launch.film).

title: Soft CTA at 60-70%, hard CTA last
statement: Put a soft CTA at 60-70% of the runtime and the hard CTA end card in the last 2.5 s (2.0 s on a 15 s ad); on a loop, replace the end card with a small tag at 0.8 opacity outside the bottom 35%.
evidence: house default [H].
notes: Set today by: patterns/ctas.json (a pack default outside mp plan). | structure_check.check_cta covers only the end-card window (story.cta_window); nothing checks the soft CTA at 60-70%. | Use urgency only if true; use the platform's CTA button for the link.

title: Treat day 2 as a fresh test
statement: Every post after launch day is graded as a fresh test with no carry-over reach expected.
evidence: After the 1.84M-view hero, day-2 posts drew 423-2,792 views, back at the account's 0.5-11K baseline.

title: Expect 1-10x followers
statement: Plan for 1-10x the account's followers in views: tier-A references span 1.2-52x (median 5.5x), and 340x happened only with a launch-hour network.
evidence: Tier-A films of rounds 7-8 ran 1.18x to 52x (median 5.5x of 9); the distribution-assisted 1.8M-view hero ran 340x.
notes: The range is measured; the 1-10x planning band is our reading of it.

title: One film for every two chats
statement: Post at least 1 story film for every 2 chat-skits, and cap chat uploads at 3-4 a week on YouTube with no near-duplicates.
evidence: team rule from own Shorts analytics: chat median 4 views vs film median 44, and 16 of 23 chat uploads got almost no feed exposure.

sources.locator: YouTube, last 28 days; How to apply

notes: Merged: Prefer story films to chat-skits: on Shorts, films had a median of 44 views vs 4 for chats (11x), with 17-29% of film viewers staying. [measured; own channel, 28 days, 1,002 views: 23 chat uploads (16 with almost no feed exposure) against a smaller set of films; on Reels one solo film got 390 views.] | Small, young channel; film count not recorded in the source.

title: Open post text with a known archetype
statement: Open the post text with one of five first-line archetypes: 'Introducing X.', a three-word title, a stake or opinion, a specific sourced number, or a prompt or question.
evidence: five recurring first-line patterns across 26 accounts; the introduce line alone appeared on 7; hashtags appeared on under 1% of posts.
notes: A number in post text needs a source; plan.lintClaims only covers on-screen digits.

title: Fix the hook before adding volume
statement: Before adding volume, check views per post on the last 10 posts and fix in order: the first 2 s, then format and length, then topic, then covers and copy; re-cut a flop's opening instead of reposting it.
evidence: The maker's own automated accounts published hundreds of videos at single-digit views per post (own analytics, one account set).

sources.locator: Measure, then fix the right thing

notes: Replays count as views on Shorts and Reels, so judge the hook by the 3 s hold, swipe-away or skip rate and average view duration, not views. Single-digit views on every post is the account rung: stop automation and stacking first. | Merged: Post at one steady slot rather than bursts, log hook rate (3 s views / impressions), average view duration, completion and sends per variant, and fix the hook and format before posting more of a format that gets almost no views. [house; house experience, not research.] | Drafting is the agent's job; publishing is always the user's action.

title: Run a series in a fixed slot
statement: Run a series in one fixed daily slot with one fixed caption template so the feed and audience learn the format.
evidence: seen on 5 of 26 accounts; the best had median views at 5.1x followers (321 followers), the highest ratio of the 26. That the template caused the reach is a reading.
notes: Copy a caption number only if you can prove it.

title: Few hashtags, per platform
statement: Use 3 hashtags on Instagram, up to 3 in a YouTube description, 3-5 on LinkedIn and TikTok, and 0-1 on X.
evidence: Pack defaults inside platform caps (Instagram caps per post; YouTube shows the first three above the title).
notes: Hashtags are labels, not the reach lever for short video.

title: Hero then numbered proof clips
statement: A launch posts one hero film, then one numbered proof clip per claim about 2 minutes apart in one sitting, and ends with a text post carrying the availability link.
evidence: A 7-post launch thread in 10 minutes: hero 1.84M views (tier A*, distribution-assisted); its 4 numbered clips 95-109K each (17.6-20.2x) falling smoothly, the shape of thread readers (tier B by rule).
notes: Resolved 21 Oct: thread vs single post is chosen by the launch: a product with 3+ separable claims posts hero + numbered proof clips in one sitting (link in the first or last reply); a founder posting one free or open tool posts once with the link inline at the end. Spacing rules apply to top-level posts only, not to replies inside the thread. | The clips worked as proof for readers already in the thread, not as reach drivers. No thread kit exists in the social-video skill yet. | Merged: On launch, post the film, then a numbered reply thread of 3-5 single-feature clips of 10-20 s each, 1-2 min apart, with the link in the first or last reply. [craft; the launch-stack skeleton was seen on 6 of 26 studied accounts (one account twice); on one, thread items drew about 100K views each against a 2.7K organic median, but its launch like rate (0.2%) leaves paid reach open.] | Known conflict: thread vs single spaced posts. Resolution (inferred, untested): spacing rules govern top-level posts; numbered replies under one launch post are one feed item. Round 9 instead suggests one capability per separate short post for a small account.

title: Test three hooks on one body
statement: Render three hook variants on one body and keep the one with the best measured 3 s hold and average view duration, instead of a predicted virality score.
evidence: Platform spec: one platform advises 3-5 creatives per ad group and another judges thumbnail tests on watch-time share; vendors' virality scores are predictions.
notes: lint_shotlist only checks that three variants exist (hook.three_variants_one_body); keeping the winner by measured 3 s hold is a manual step. | The three variants are enforced; the measurement loop (social-video log) is not.

title: Tell real people before the hour
statement: Before posting, tell real people personally so genuine quote posts can land in the first 70 minutes; never pay, script or pod them.
evidence: In the 1.8M-view launch from a 5.4K-follower account, 37 of 54 loaded quotes landed within 70 minutes with 1.49M views between them (measured); that the wave caused the reach is inference, and payment is unknown.
notes: The top amplifier wore the company's own affiliate badge; investors and a partner pre-post (22 min early) also took part.

title: Judge posts by saves, not views
statement: Read a post's result by its bookmark rate (saves-strong at 1.3% or more) and, for proven organic, 1.5x+ followers with 1.5%+ bookmarks and 0.2%+ likes, not by raw views.
evidence: A round-3 launch with a celebrity gained 40% more views than its sibling with the same bookmarks; the best-saved round-3 piece reached 3.8% bookmarks at 1.9x.
notes: tools/refstudy.py grade applies these rates to reference studies only; nothing reads our own posts yet. | Merged: Grade a post as strong only at views per follower >= 1.5 or bookmarks >= 1.5% of views, with a like rate >= 0.2%; never on one big view count. [house; the pack's tier rule; in round 9 two tier-A posts sat on the knife edge at 1.51% and 1.60% bookmarks.] | refstudy grade assigns the tier; it does not fail a build. | Merged: Judge each post at 48 h on bookmark and like rate per view, with bookmarks of 1.3% or more as the strong signal, never on raw views. [measured-A; Tier-A films ran 0.13-2.20% bookmarks and 0.26-2.22% likes; the 1.8M-view hero had more bookmarks than likes (0.23% vs 0.20%).] | tools/refstudy.py grade applies the tier rules (A- = bookmark rate 1.3%+), but no pack check runs on our own posts.

title: Launch between 12:30 and 16:00 UTC
statement: Post launch films between 12:30 and 16:00 UTC.
evidence: 9 of 10 timed reference launches landed in this window (the 10th at 08:58 UTC); it reflects who was studied, not a tested optimum.

evidence: The two founder tier-A posts of round 7 were free or open tools with a link (bookmarks 0.89% and 2.20%).

evidence: Practitioner belief that body links cut reach on X and LinkedIn (not published); Instagram caption links are not clickable (platform spec).

title: Looping Short: tag, not card

title: Post less when nobody is seeing it
statement: When median views per post are under about 20, cut to 1-2 originals a day and spend the freed time on manual replies.
evidence: one studied account posting 8 a day had a 14.5-view median; a 13-a-day rewritten-news account earned about 250 views per post.

title: Teardown first, then launch within a week
statement: Publish a genuinely useful teardown of a big move in your category, then launch into that attention within 7 days.
evidence: one founder: a 412,511-view teardown with 4,501 bookmarks (1.09%), then a 1.86M-view launch 7 days later; n = 1.
notes: Volume newsjacking without a useful angle did not work on another account (about 250 views each).

title: Re-angle the launch, then post BTS
statement: On day +1 quote-post your own launch with a new angle (a partner, a changelog, a use), and post a behind-the-scenes of making the film 3-4 days after launch.
evidence: one account ran this on two launches a month apart; another quote-posted its launch with a full changelog 23 min after launch; in launch week executives also quoted outside reviewers instead of repeating claims.

sources.locator: 3. Recycling a launch video; per-account notes, video-to-sound startup and big-tech executives

title: Never batch-post videos on one platform
statement: Post at most 1 video per platform per hour; a batch of 5 Reels posted in 9 minutes decayed 112, 124, 52, 17, 7 views, while one film posted alone the same month got 390.
evidence: own channel analytics over 30 days: one 5-post batch against one solo post (n = 1 each), small account.

sources.locator: Instagram, last 30 days; How to apply

notes: skills/social-video/SKILL.md 'Scheduling vs posting everywhere at once' already says never two in the same hour (prose). Whether numbered replies under one launch post count as a batch is untested.

title: Builder films end on URL, no spoken ask
statement: For builder audiences end on a URL, repo or typed install command on the end card with no spoken CTA, and keep the price and the argument in the post copy.
evidence: round 4/5: no tier-A explainer had a spoken CTA; a URL or repo end card was the tier-A norm.

sources.locator: 9. CTA and end; 6. CTA and end

title: Number each clip post by problem

evidence: All 4 clip posts of a 1.8M-view launch thread follow this copy shape (tier B by rule, read as C).

title: One change per test, rule first

statement: Leave at least 4 h between two top-level posts on the same platform.
evidence: team rule set after the measured batch decay (5 posts in 9 min fell to 7 views); the 4 h value itself was not A/B tested.

title: Reply by hand in one voice
statement: Genuine replies get hand-written answers in one consistent voice over the first 36 hours.
evidence: The 1.8M-view launch replied to about 65 of 440 replies over a day and a half in one playful voice.

title: Answer every reply in the first hour
statement: Stay after posting and answer every reply within 60 min, aiming for under 15 min, literally and including 'not yet' answers.
evidence: 4 founder accounts replied in 1-50 min (one 8 min to 2 h with plain 'not yet' answers); fast repliers show more replies per view, but cause and effect cannot be separated.
notes: skills/social-video/SKILL.md says X is better posted live by a person who stays to reply (prose).

title: Self-repost the launch once
statement: Self-repost the launch post once, about 8 h after posting, for the next time-zone peak.
evidence: 5 of 26 accounts self-repost launches, one at 3-4 time-zone peaks; the 8 h value is a plan choice.

title: Titles: stake first, 50 characters
statement: Titles run about 50 characters or fewer (100 max on YouTube), lead with the stake or the payoff in searchable words, and never open with the product name, a series label or all caps.
evidence: Pack copy default; titles matter most for search, channel pages and suggested videos, not the feed.

sources.locator: YouTube; Titles: patterns that keep the promise

title: One useful post beats many rewrites
statement: Prefer one useful post that names real people (a list, a teardown) over high-volume rewrites: rewritten news earned about 250 views each while useful lists reached 4,300-18,400.
evidence: one account, 199 own posts: median 304 views; 5 of its top 6 own posts were list posts.
notes: n = 1 account; named people have a reason to share, which is the inferred mechanism.

title: One UTM convention everywhere
statement: Tag every off-site link utm_source=<platform>, utm_medium=<surface>, utm_campaign=<series-or-release>, utm_content=<video-slug>[-a|-b|-c], lowercase and hyphenated, with a separate utm_source for AI-assistant referrals and no UTMs on links inside your own site.
evidence: Pack analytics convention; internal UTMs waste crawl and double-count.
